How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. Who are the holders of 5% or more of Varonis stock today, and who will hold controlling interests in the combined company if the Proofpoint acquisition closes?
    A bank needs to know who controls the vendor, particularly while a change of control is pending.
  2. Has Varonis had any security incident affecting its corporate systems or SaaS platform in the last five years, and how were customers notified?
    A security vendor's own incident record indicates how well it protects the access it is given to bank data.
  3. Which customers did not renew on-premises subscriptions in 2025, what reasons did they give, and what share of self-hosted customers has moved to SaaS ahead of the 31 December 2026 end of life?
    Loss of major customers can signal product or service problems.
  4. Have there been any executive departures, governance disputes or findings against Varonis officers in the last three years, and what officer changes are planned under the Proofpoint agreement?
    Leadership disputes or departures can affect delivery and governance.
  5. What is the pricing metric and list price for the Varonis Data Security Platform, Atlas AI Security, Interceptor and MDDR, and how will pricing be treated after the Proofpoint transaction?
    Pricing structure affects total cost and the terms of exit.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-11 · launch Varonis Systems
    Varonis adds LLM Gateway and MCP Gateway to Atlas AI Security

    The Varonis changelog records the release of an LLM Gateway for controlling AI model usage and spend and an MCP Gateway for governing agent tool access, both within Atlas AI Security, followed on 12 November by an Agent Manifest feature. Varonis (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-10-15 · acquisition ProofpointVaronis Systems
    Proofpoint agrees to acquire Varonis for US$49.75 per share in cash, about US$6.3 billion

    Proofpoint and Varonis announced a merger agreement on 15 October 2026 under which Proofpoint would pay US$49.75 per share in cash, about US$6.3 billion. As of 20 November 2026 the deal had not closed. Varonis filed its definitive merger proxy on 16 November 2026: the stockholder vote is set for 22 December 2026, a US antitrust filing was made on 19 October 2026, clearances are also required in Australia, France, Italy, Luxembourg and the United Kingdom, and closing is expected in the first half of 2027, with a termination date of 15 July 2027 that can be extended by three months. Funding is about US$3.86 billion of equity from Thoma Bravo funds and up to US$1.25 billion of debt; the merger has no financing condition. The companies operate separately until closing.
